author: Krystal Montez
title: What Causes Mosquitoes to Target Certain People? Scent, Science, and Oil - NewsBreak
text:
By Krystal Montez ,
2 hours ago
If you’ve ever felt like mosquitoes skip a whole crowd just to turn you into a buffet, you’re not crazy, and you’re definitely not alone.
Growing up on the West Coast, I always seemed to attract a bite or two. But moving to Louisiana ? That was a whole different story. Here, mosquitoes will ignore every single person around me, lock in on my skin, and leave me with welts so massive I hesitate to even put on shorts.
As it turns out, it’s not about your hygiene, it’s all about your personal skin signature.
According to experts cited by Science Alert , mosquitoes really do target certain people over others. Medical entomologist Frederic Simard explains that our skin’s microbiota creates a unique “soup of molecules” that acts like a scent signature. Out of up to 1,000 odorous compounds our bodies release, scientists like Rickard Ignell found that mosquitoes hone in on a specific blend, especially a compound formed from the natural breakdown of skin oils.
To make matters worse for us patio lovers, that cold beer might be working against you. Research shows that drinking beer raises body temperature, increases exhaled CO2, and alters skin odor. In fact, a study in the Netherlands found that participants who drank beer within the last 24 hours were 1.35 times more attractive to malaria-carrying mosquitoes.
But let’s be real: saying no to a cold beer in this Louisiana heat feels like a sin. Heading to The 7th Tap in the East Bank District and ordering a smash burger without that ice-cold brew, the kind that makes anyone smile through the humidity, just isn’t going to happen.
So if you’re looking to dodge the swarm, maybe we just load up on the bug spray before hitting our local brewery. Either that or opt for straight tequila, science didn’t mention it, and hey, we’re keeping things healthy, right?
